NFL DFS Tight End Rankings: Week 12 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 29 · 9 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of November 24, 10:02 PM ET

Trey McBride is the top-projected tight end on the Week 12 DraftKings main slate at 16.6 DraftKings points for $6,600, against Washington. George Kittle (12.7, $6,500) and Isaiah Likely (12.5, $5,900) are next.

T.J. Hockenson returns the most per dollar among tight ends projected for at least 7 points: 2.67 projected points per $1,000 at $4,300.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the November 24, 10:02 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Tight ends to know in Week 12

Trey McBride, ARI vs WAS ($6,600)

Trey McBride carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 16.6 DraftKings points at $6,600. That is 4.0 points clear of George Kittle. The model gives him 11.1 targets on 33.4 routes. The salary works out to 2.52 projected points per $1,000, 2nd of 12 at the position. Across 50,000 simulations McBride averaged 16.7 points with a simulated floor of 3.9 and a ceiling of 42.7, and he holds 18% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Arizona is a 7-point underdog at home against Washington, with an implied team total of 17.25 in a game totaled at 41.5.

George Kittle, SF vs SEA ($6,500)

George Kittle projects 2nd at the position with 12.7 DraftKings points at $6,500. The model gives him 5.7 targets on 22.6 routes. The salary works out to 1.95 projected points per $1,000, 10th of 12 at the position. Across 50,000 simulations Kittle averaged 12.6 points with a simulated floor of 1.9 and a ceiling of 34.1, and he holds 6% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. San Francisco is a 3.5-point favorite at home against Seattle, with an implied team total of 24.5 in a game totaled at 45.5.

Value: Greg Dulcich, MIA vs NYJ ($2,900)

Greg Dulcich projects for 7.2 DraftKings points at $2,900, which works out to 2.49 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 12 tight ends the model projects for 7 or more points. The model gives him 4.1 targets on 18.4 routes. Across 50,000 simulations Dulcich averaged 7.2 points with a simulated floor of 0.0 and a ceiling of 29.0, and he holds 12% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Miami is a 3.5-point underdog at home against the Jets, with an implied team total of 18.5 in a game totaled at 40.5.
